rules.observation: Repeated prefill.decode_interval with waiting_requests>0 or chunk_pending=1, while per-rank prefill service is insufficient.
rules.diagnosis: The configured decode interval explicitly prevents the admission scan. Free KV or absent budget-gate events do not rule this out.
alternatives: Queued requests may also be ineligible for cache transfer or capacity.
Another DP rank can arm the interval; local queue pressure may differ.
A graph-to-eager transition lengthens scheduler steps, reducing wall-clock prefill opportunities at the same configured countdown; this is distinct from a change in interval value.
rules.check: Correlate rank-local gate windows with queue slope, prefill effective-token rates, decode output rate and resolved cadence. Event counts do not measure wait time. Compare decode graph/non-graph and prefill step rates in the same retained spans. The countdown advances per scheduling call and is rearmed on synchronized extend work, not by a wall-clock timer. Stable step ratios with slower steps can explain less prefill service without a new token-budget limit.
rules.action: If eligible work is repeatedly deferred by cadence and useful prefill service is insufficient, test one cadence change. If dispatch coverage slows all scheduler opportunities, resolve graph eligibility first. Retain latency and closed-loop workload confounders.
rules.expected: Fewer consecutive deferrals and higher prefill service; decode ITL may worsen.
rules.reject_if: Output throughput or p10 user speed regresses without a useful Pareto tradeoff; gate evidence does not clear.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Queued work with input/chunk budget encounters and available KV; explicit interval and request caps are not the dominant obstruction.
rules.diagnosis: A prefill compute budget stops further admission, but the first emitted gate does not uniquely identify a configuration knob: input exhaustion precedes chunk exhaustion.
alternatives: Replay rows consume the same budget.
DP divides declared chunk size.
Post-admission checks are not rejected requests.
Input and chunk limits can exhaust together; raising max_prefill_tokens alone may change only the gate name.
Normal chunked shape selection uses chunk/KV limits, so max_prefill_tokens is not a universal per-forward hard ceiling.
Larger effective chunks require sufficient MegaMoE token capacity and symmetric-buffer memory.
rules.check: Read resolved per-rank input/chunk limits and prefill.admitted residuals together. Inspect gate order and the actual normal/chunk-continuation path. Check aligned chunk size against the MegaMoE env cap and physical memory before proposing a larger budget. Where deployed, join pass_end.adder_stop_site to the same ending/residuals. existing_chunk_slot with positive residuals identifies the one-continuation return branch; pass_input_budget with both exhausted identifies the ordered input check, not evidence that raising input alone helps. Missing/unannotated sites stay unknown.
rules.action: If input/chunk budget genuinely limits useful prefill, test a coherent compute/workspace budget. If only the first named gate shifts, retain capacity and inspect downstream admission.
rules.expected: Larger useful admitted batches and increased prefill service, potentially worse TTFT/ITL.
rules.reject_if: Service does not improve, memory guard trips, or long-context coverage/errors worsen.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Request-slot encounters and a growing queue while device capacity remains available.
rules.diagnosis: Admission encountered a row/PP-count constraint, which may be an intentional tradeoff that protects graph coverage rather than an undersized knob.
alternatives: An earlier gate can hide a later memory limit.
Increasing active rows can exceed decode graph capture coverage.
For DSV4, changing row capacity also changes fixed-state/SWA sizing and may change device FULL plus ratio-sized host retention. Read sizing logs before interpreting a pure admission effect.
rules.check: Compare resolved row and PP microbatch limits, running/held/beam rows, graph-use service and the canonical throughput/latency tradeoff. The aggregate gate merges pre-sort and candidate-loop sites and does not identify the minimum budget component. A sampled maximum below the cap does not exclude transient saturation.
rules.action: If row pressure accompanies useful advancing owners, test capacity with graph/memory bounds. If owners stall or remain after cancellation, diagnose progress/cleanup before raising capacity.
rules.expected: More active work, if another gate does not replace this one.
rules.reject_if: KV gates/retractions immediately replace the row gate or latency worsens without useful throughput.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: FULL/SWA/shared-capacity failures during queued work, or retractions under sustained load.
rules.diagnosis: The effective device-pool geometry or reservations cannot fit the workload.
alternatives: Locked prefixes and future output reservation differ from physical usage.
Graph buffers, draft state and replay tails consume memory.
Wrapper memory_budget can duplicate a lower-level gate.
rules.check: Compare startup actual capacities, per-pool evictable/available tokens and reservation observations. Do not add wrapper and allocator events.
rules.action: If actual pool capacity blocks otherwise eligible service, test one memory tradeoff. If allocator reserved bytes alone rise, do not infer a pool shortage.
rules.expected: Capacity gate clears without OOM/retraction or excessive recomputation.
rules.reject_if: Measured capacity does not change or another physical pool still binds.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Eager dispatch grows under high active batch sizes despite a configured decode graph runner.
rules.diagnosis: Decode/verify graph coverage may be insufficient, but the eager counter also includes prefill and idle paths.
alternatives: Prefill is deliberately eager in the baseline.
Target versus draft and graph eligibility predicates differ.
A runner receipt does not prove every layer replayed.
Sampled local running-request counts can miss transient or DP-wide graph input sizes; non-size eligibility gates can fail below the configured cap.
rules.check: Use existing CUDA graph counters with producer-defined labels and actual phase context; obtain mode-specific dispatch evidence before attributing eager events to decode. In DSpark, decode-result eligibility comes from target verification, not all draft passes or layer-tail replay. Trace decode_cuda_graph_runner.can_run_graph before attributing a fallback to max_bs: overrides, layout/width, supported shape, DP eligibility, encoder, TBO and ngram conditions can reject it. DP gather can use the maximum DP batch size rather than a sampled local request gauge. Preserve absent lazy-created series as unknown; count fractions do not establish exposed time.
rules.action: If lost graph coverage slows service, test a supported row/shape eligibility repair. If coverage is healthy, retain graph settings and inspect other mechanisms.
rules.expected: Relevant graph replay recovers with useful token service and acceptable canonical throughput/latency; a row-cap trial may trade batch parallelism for faster steps.
rules.reject_if: Replay does not recover, the unsupported size/gate remains, or lost batch parallelism/KV retention makes the qualified throughput/latency tradeoff worse.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Full C256 baseline has modest sustained active batches and queues, sampled max40/rank versus resolved96 request cap, and no request/KV-capacity encounters in covered windows.
rules.diagnosis: At this load point, offered trajectory work may limit useful batch work. Spare request rows do not by themselves prove spare GPU compute or physical memory.
alternatives: Workload trace lengths differ by lane.
Queue depletion can be caused by a slow upstream stage.
Router prefix approximation differs from server radix-cache state.
Prefill compute budget, CPU/synchronization critical path or graph coverage may limit scaling.
Additional lanes enlarge the cache working set and change closed-loop replay progress.

Changing trajectory concurrency changes canonical warmup volume and retained cache at profiling start. Preserve the preset; compare full workload/cache histories before attributing a gain to batching alone.
rules.check: Inspect the deployed router implementation, routing headers, client offered load, HTTP activity, per-rank arrivals and tier hit rates.
rules.action: If fresh empty worker queues coexist with offered demand, inspect routing/supply. If queues are occupied, inspect admission/service before increasing client pressure.
rules.expected: More useful active work and higher full-run throughput, with possible ITL/user-speed cost. Confirm complete canonical score and Pareto position; do not assume linear scaling.
rules.reject_if: Full throughput does not improve while queue/latency grows, active work fails to rise, or cache/graph/prefill/capacity effects explain lost scaling.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

external_controls.name: AgentX --concurrency
external_controls.note: Load-point axis external to SGLang server configuration; changing this does not raise server max_running_requests.

rules.observation: Host-table startup shows lower huge-page coverage on some ranks, optionally with a MADV_COLLAPSE error. Preserve the actual errno; do not assume all failures share a cause.
rules.diagnosis: Actual table backing differs despite identical layout settings; address translation and placement may confound rank latency.
alternatives: Concurrent snapshot persistence/checksum or loader reads repopulate file cache.
NUMA-local contiguous memory or process affinity differs.
The workload may not expose host lookups enough for coverage to matter.
New-node backing skew persists even with staging complete: allocator fragmentation or loader-local pressure remains possible; staging concurrency is not a sufficient explanation.
rules.check: Read per-layer/rank coverage, /proc scheduler affinity and NUMA placement, host/cgroup headroom and staging completion. Correlate with matched-rank forward latency before attribution.
rules.action: If backing/placement differs across candidates, match or stratify it before attributing a gain. If matched repeatability holds, assess the intervention on its measured outcome.
rules.expected: If temporary staging pressure caused the backing skew, coverage may improve without a serving-config change.
rules.reject_if: Coverage stays skewed or improves without a latency benefit; do not claim a scheduler bottleneck or host-lookup speedup from the receipt alone.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Decoder tail graph capture receipts while whole-prefill cuda_graph mode is prefill_none, with early warmup service variation.
rules.diagnosis: Layer-tail graphs are enabled independently of whole-prefill graph dispatch and capture lazily. Cold capture overhead is part of this window.
alternatives: Cold prefix misses require real prefill work. Client reconstruction, request arrival skew and host-table backing can also alter early rates.
rules.check: Read capture timestamps/cumulative seconds and client phase together with per-rank useful prefill counters. Whole-forward none does not imply all layers are eager.
rules.action: If warmup contains previously unseen capture work, preserve canonical warmup and inspect capture coverage. If steady state is covered, do not extrapolate startup stalls into serving cost.
rules.expected: Cold capture receipts taper as shapes are covered; steady-state benefit requires paired evidence.
rules.reject_if: Capture continues for new shapes, or useful rates do not stabilize; no conclusion from gate counts alone.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Three early profiling windows have small batches and near-empty queues; later canonical idle-cap advances coincide with more long requests and larger queues.
rules.diagnosis: Offered work changes within the profiling phase. Early consistent windows can still represent only a light-load regime.
alternatives: Client CPU/transport saturation; routing skew; server admission limits. Check client CPU and per-rank arrivals/gates rather than assuming one.

Changing trajectory concurrency changes canonical warmup volume and retained cache at profiling start. Preserve the preset; compare full workload/cache histories before attributing a gain to batching alone.
rules.check: Align benchmark phase and idle-cap events with request-length distributions, active batches, queues, cache rates and admission events.
rules.action: If realized request/cache mix changes across windows, compare full canonical trajectories and matched repeats. If workload matches, test the source-backed mechanism prediction.
rules.expected: A useful diagnosis remains supported after accounting for offered-load changes; measured server bottlenecks recur under comparable pressure.
rules.reject_if: Pressure shifts invalidate the earlier diagnosis, or a different gate appears. Reopen the hypothesis before applying a change.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Similar input-length strata have radically different TTFT across AgentX elapsed-time bins; optional per-request cached-token usage is missing.
rules.diagnosis: Input length is not computed prefill work. Cache reuse, transfers and changing trajectory mix can mimic a cadence or compute-cap effect.
alternatives: Actual scheduling/cadence or host restoration may still explain latency.
Live completed-record samples exclude unfinished long-tail requests.
rules.check: Use finalized elapsed-time/length strata, server tier counters and phase accounting. Enable per-request cache reporting in a separately recorded instrumentation trial when aggregate evidence cannot discriminate.
rules.action: If the required input/cache-cost producer is activated and complete, compare observed cost proxies. If absent, run a bounded activation check before drawing conclusions.
rules.reject_if: Reporting remains absent, changes token accounting, adds unacceptable overhead, or cache-conditioned evidence does not support the proposed mechanism.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.
rules.expected: Optional cached-token field becomes available while logical token counts and workload rules stay unchanged.

rules.observation: Host-cache occupancy grows beyond the first15minutes while device eviction/backups continue; device-without-backup drop counters remain zero in observed windows.
rules.diagnosis: Device eviction may be normal tier migration. Full/L2 working-set pressure is plausible later, but neither low activeKV usage nor zero device-drop counters proves spare retention capacity.
alternatives: Context/branch mix and routing can change cache reuse without a capacity limit.
Host restore or blocking backup may matter even when data is retained.
Cache TP coordinates differ from scheduler TP coordinates under DPattention.
DSV4 generic host-used/total gauges measure logical FULL anchors, which own no KV tensor; compressed/SWA physical pools and total host RAM are not represented by that percentage.
rules.check: Preserve DP/attentionTP/pool labels; compare available/evictable/used tokens, host occupancy, computed versus cached input, drop deltas and operation-duration deltas across the full replay. Do not add overlapping eviction/backup durations. DeepSeek V4 derives host pages from device page capacities times hicache_ratio and rejects positive hicache_size. A lower static-memory fraction can shrink both device and ratio-sized host retention if it lowers resolved pool capacity. Inspect actual capacities and physical bytes; a compensating ratio need not preserve all side pools.
rules.action: If useful reuse exceeds measured exposed migration cost, retain cache. If copy/eviction timers include waits, identify their owners before choosing CPU or bandwidth work.
rules.expected: A true retention limitation should show late reuse/recompute changes or host eviction evidence; added host-eviction observation distinguishes ordinary L2 eviction from unbacked device drops.
rules.reject_if: Workload/routing changes explain the signal, transfers are not exposed, or no retention benefit remains after matching relevant regimes. Zero device-drop counts alone cannot reject ordinary L2 eviction.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: DP imbalance/synchronization histograms remain zero while scheduler stage labels show forward_overlap=none.
rules.diagnosis: These values may reflect disabled producers and unavailable device timing, rather than balanced ranks or exposed CPU bottlenecks.
alternatives: Enabled producer with no eligible multi-rank gather or only health probes.
Rank-local reporting restrictions.
Actual low imbalance or low synchronization cost requires positive count coverage.
rules.check: Inspect explicit launch controls and in-process resolved producer values where available; source defaults are context. A missing /proc/PID/environ entry does not prove unset: setproctitle can overwrite that memory while Python getenv retains the value. Verify eligible paths, reporting ranks and positive histogram count deltas. Stage wall time includes waiting; endpoint overlap labels do not measure exposed GPU gaps.
rules.action: If the observation contract is fresh and active, interpret its zero within its scope. If not, repair activation or report unknown before another expensive experiment.
rules.expected: Positive eligible count coverage and interpretable rank-local observations; unchanged serving work must be independently checked.
rules.reject_if: Counts remain absent, coverage is inadequate, or instrumentation changes performance enough to confound the comparison.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: A fresh deployment fails to load a Rust TreeCore binding, or reports a different constructed TreeCore despite matched source/configuration.
rules.diagnosis: Backend resolution depends on toolchain availability, build mode and extension visibility beyond tracked Python source.
alternatives: Unsupported cache components/platform can intentionally fall back to Python.
Different inherited environment, source-overlay native artifacts or compiler workspace can change selection.
rules.check: Compare prior per-rank Init Unified Radix Cache/Tree Core lines. Check compiler queries in the source-defined workspace, requested backend/buildmode, binding import spec and effective source path.
rules.action: If the resolved backend and matched native tests support a change, compare interleaved canonical repeats. If host backing/workload differs, keep attribution unresolved.
rules.expected: Matched constructed class and successful initialization; no throughput gain is inferred from backend naming.
rules.reject_if: Resolved backend still differs, construction fails, or compatibility tests fail; never substitute an arbitrary binary just to bypass startup.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Persistent mixed-work queues and long first-forward waits coexist with many fast requests; client TTFT tails are much longer than connection/send overhead.
rules.diagnosis: Admission ordering may repeatedly favor inexpensive uncached work. Shortest-prefill-first uses age only as a tie-breaker; initial queue waits are distinct from later chunk execution and router delay.
alternatives: Cadence, token/capacity gates or cache readiness can delay admission independent of sorting.
An increase in observed long waits can mean old backlog is finally being admitted; still-waiting requests remain censored.
Closed-loop trajectory progress and cache locality change with policy; total input length is not uncached work.

Shortest-prefill-first uniquely reserves continuation budget for shorter waiting requests and gates the chunk-slot event. HRRN removes that reservation, so a single policy flag changes more than sorting; absent chunk-slot events under HRRN are expected producer semantics.
rules.check: Use source-defined queue histogram bucket/count/sum deltas by rank and observation time, plus finalized client request-start strata and cancellations. The sampled shortest_uncached log describes the first sorted request, not the oldest. Verify HRRN processed-token arrival/accounting path before proposing it. HRRN age advances with processed prefill tokens, not wall time; inspect queue-entry/requeue snapshots. Record continuation-reservation changes and event producer conditions before comparison. Distinguish current queue-episode perf_counter age from submitted-token age and actual readiness: sorting precedes budget/prefetch/staging checks. Unified reentry resets both age origins. HRRN and SPF estimate output-bearing work differently; establish its incidence before using that difference to explain performance. Verify tuning_policy_config and sample coverage by rank. Read queue snapshots, visit outcomes and continuation separately; candidates not visited have unknown readiness, and a selected head is not necessarily admitted. Compare paired age/work within the same record. Snapshot counts are not request arrival rates or wait seconds. Configured HRRN falls back to FCFS above128waiting requests. Check effective_policy and queue_snapshot_available before interpreting sort-derived fields; candidate work retains the configured-policy estimate. Source fallback alone does not establish R7 incidence. A visit labeled admitted can still end the pass with OTHER/NO_TOKEN. Use optional pass_end when deployed; pass_budget_stop counts only the pre-candidate gate and must not be treated as all budget-limited passes. Missing pass_end is unknown; adder categories do not isolate KV/input/chunk causes.
rules.action: If old eligible requests are repeatedly bypassed, test an ordering/fairness repair. If they wait for decode reservation or readiness, repair that dependency first.
rules.expected: An aging/order change should alter which work is admitted, reduce persistent old backlog or improve finalized tails, with possible loss of prefix locality and throughput.
rules.reject_if: No improvement in finalized tails/backlog or trajectory progress, or unacceptable loss of qualified total/output throughput or latency Pareto position. Do not accept based only on fewer emitted long-wait observations.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: GPU management snapshots show very little free memory, possibly without corresponding KV admission failures.
rules.diagnosis: Physical usage is not decomposed by logical KV utilization or the configured static fraction. Live tensors, reserved allocator blocks, graph/private pools and external symmetric buffers are competing contributors.
alternatives: A large reserved footprint may coexist with reusable blocks; reserved minus allocated is not guaranteed reclaimable.
PyTorch stats may exclude custom/private pools and external library allocations.
Request shape, startup history and lazy capture differ across ranks and runs.
Native high-water counters can predate the observed quarter or be reset by another caller. Distinct peak fields need not coincide; their sum is not peak memory usage.
rules.check: Retain timestamped GPU samples and resolved pool capacities. On a later validated deployment, enable the optional native-allocator snapshot and inspect allocated/reserved/active bytes plus same-process retry/OOM counter deltas. Unsupported, missing and error statuses remain unknown. Use actual buffer-creation receipts for external allocation provenance. Size external buffers with the resolved aligned cap. Retire earlier unaligned API estimates as actual allocation or headroom evidence; no corrected baseline delta was measured by this probe. If considering less static KV allocation to create runtime slack, trace the actual sizing path and account for ratio-sized host retention; lower logical KV occupancy does not establish that lost prefix retention is free.
rules.action: If fixed pool capacity blocks service, inspect geometry; if transient allocator peaks cause OOM, inspect workspace. Neither a peak nor a frequent gate alone establishes recoverable throughput.
rules.expected: Allocator snapshots distinguish supported native allocator counters from unknown external/pool contributions; a later headroom intervention should reduce actual allocation failures without an unacceptable capacity/throughput loss.
rules.reject_if: Snapshot coverage/backend is unknown, observation changes behavior materially, or only a reserved-memory subtraction supports the claimed cause.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Startup stops before weight loading; some ranks emit PIL fallback but another remains in an optional cargo version subprocess.
rules.diagnosis: The optional auto image-backend probe can invoke Rustup toolchain setup. Other ranks may wait for the blocked rank even on a text-only workload.
alternatives: Distributed initialization, weight I/O, compilation, or loader errors can also leave quiet logs; confirm the exact child and source interval.
rules.check: Inspect actual per-rank milestones and the owned cargo child command, parent and executable. Missing fallback warning is unknown, not success. No throughput diagnosis follows from this startup delay.
rules.action: If optional dependency probing blocks startup, select a supported explicit backend and validate native startup. If healthy, preserve the control.
rules.expected: The optional Rust image probe is bypassed and startup reaches weight loading without waiting for toolchain installation. No throughput gain is claimed.
rules.reject_if: The stall is elsewhere, PIL is rejected, effective backend differs, or image-input semantics are required and have not been validated.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Startup reports an unsupported backend/PD/graph combination before benchmark traffic.
rules.diagnosis: The model-specific compatibility checks reject the configuration; this is not evidence of insufficient queue capacity or memory.
alternatives: Generic parser acceptance can precede model-specific rejection.
Changing an attention backend also changes kernel/layout behavior; topology is not the only intervention.
rules.check: Read the exact validator and resolved model/backend/role/graph settings. Distinguish startup selection receipts from executed-forward telemetry.
rules.action: If source guards and native transfer tests support the topology, proceed to canonical validation. If a path is unsupported, select a compatible alternative before model startup.
rules.expected: A compatible configuration passes startup validation; correctness and throughput remain separate tests.
rules.reject_if: Model validation, target/draft KV agreement, transfer correctness or canonical replay fails.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: The launch flag is disabled, or enabled without any distinct serving branch receipt.
rules.diagnosis: Fusion is a candidate mechanism, but launch settings alone do not establish eligibility, execution incidence, correctness or benefit.
alternatives: Collective planning or a missing/incompatible next boundary prevents dispatch.
The pinned library lacks the required API or fails numeric/capture checks.
Fusion is reached but does not dominate the measured workload; optional quantization or decode paths change the tradeoff.

A synthetic probe that switches GPUs after initializing context-local library state may fail even when the serving process topology works; reproduce the actual process/device ownership before changing model code.
rules.check: Trace the reached branch, mode and shape. Validate checkpoint-weight shifted ordering, BF16 rounding, next statistics, optional MXFP8 output and per-stream warmup/capture on the pinned GPU library. Keep synthetic correctness separate from actual model quality and serving selection. Existing --enable-profile-cuda-graph plus SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_CAPTURE_TRACE can export actual startup kernel traces; verify their contents and runner/rank/timing coverage instead of treating an export log as kernel evidence.
rules.action: If native dispatch/accuracy passes and matched canonical repeats improve the target, retain the candidate. If the full result regresses or confounders dominate, retain the reference or repeat with matched controls.
rules.expected: A compatible kernel passes numerical and capture checks; actual selection receipts and full replay then test whether useful service and canonical throughput improve.
rules.reject_if: Numeric/API/capture checks fail, actual serving selection cannot be established, or the full candidate regresses the intended throughput/latency objective.
rules.status: Conditional source-backed rule; current applicability and decisions are in canonical campaign outcomes and decisions/current.json.

rules.observation: Persistent admission pressure with fresh correlated owner/waiter records.
rules.diagnosis: Use stage, age, actual resource acquisition/release and readiness facts to separate useful capacity pressure from stalled or cancelled ownership.
alternatives: Missing peer records, sampling/loss or stale snapshots leave attribution unresolved.
Host receive, rebootstrap, chunk continuation and session retention are valid branches.
rules.check: Require tested phase activation and native consumer reconstruction. Compare each process only with its own monotonic clock; observe pool availability and exceptional entries. Never equate an inclusive timer with exposed CPU work.
rules.action: If young holders advance, test capacity versus useful service. If holders stall or remain after cancellation, repair progress/cleanup. If history is incomplete, resolve that diagnostic dependency before repeating full performance trials.
rules.expected: An observation changes the chosen action or explicitly leaves attribution unresolved; completeness alone is not a speedup.
rules.reject_if: Consumer cannot reconstruct the native zero-forward stall or actual release/reuse, required contracts are stale, or overhead/defaults are unmeasured.
rules.status: Native lifecycle qualification is pending in campaign records; this source map does not assert it passed.

policy: Source-backed conditional rules are not causal performance predictions. Historical narratives are archived separately; immutable experiment predictions and canonical outcomes own empirical results. Current operational state belongs only to decisions/current.json.
